manifest_record.title: Finite-field points of the semistable quiver stack give the Hall groupoid

references.title: Tom Bridgeland, Hall algebras and Donaldson–Thomas invariants, §§2.1 and 4.4
Tom Bridgeland, An Introduction to Motivic Hall Algebras, §§3.1–3.2

manifest_record.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the semistable-openness prerequisite.
Let $Q$ be finite and acyclic over $k=\mathbb F_q$, and let
$\mathbf d\in\mathbb N^{Q_0}$. The rational-point groupoid of
$\mathfrak M^{ss}_{\mathbf d}(Q,Z)$ is finite and is equivalent to the
groupoid whose objects are $Z$-semistable $\mathbb F_q$-representations of
dimension $\mathbf d$ and whose arrows are their representation isomorphisms.
Its groupoid cardinality is therefore
$$\sum_{[M]:\,\mathbf d(M)=\mathbf d,\ M\;Z\text{-semistable}} \frac{1}{|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathcal A_Q}(M)|}.$$

manifest_record.title: The principal nilpotent Borel orbit by height elimination
manifest_record.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the setup of
[[def-complex-semisimple-algebraic-group-borel-and-flag-variety]]. For each
simple root $\alpha_i$ choose a nonzero root vector $e_i\in\mathfrak g_{\alpha_i}$
and put $e=\sum_i e_i$. Write
$\mathfrak n^+_j=\bigoplus_{\operatorname{ht}(\alpha)=j}\mathfrak g_\alpha$.
Then
$$B\cdot e=\left\{\sum_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}c_\alpha e_\alpha\in\mathfrak n^+: c_{\alpha_i}\ne0\text{ for every simple root }\alpha_i\right\},$$
where one nonzero $e_\alpha\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$ is fixed for each positive
root. The right side is independent of the choices of those root vectors.

manifest_record.title: PBW and integral line-bundle twisting for flag TDOs
manifest_record.statement:
Use $X$, $\mathfrak g$, $\mathfrak b_X$, and $\mathcal D_\kappa$ from
[[def-pa36-flag-tdo-and-module]]. For every $\kappa\in\mathfrak h^*$ the
isotropy relations generate a two-sided ideal and define a TDO satisfying
$$F_0\mathcal D_\kappa=\mathcal O_X,\qquad \operatorname{gr}\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Sym}_{\mathcal O_X}T_X.$$
If $\eta\in X^*(T)$ is integral, then
$$\mathcal D_\kappa\cong\operatorname{Diff}\bigl(\mathcal O_X(\kappa+\rho)\bigr) \quad(\kappa+\rho\text{ integral}),\qquad \mathcal D_{-\rho}=\operatorname{Diff}(\mathcal O_X),$$
and tensoring by $\mathcal O_X(\eta)$ defines an equivalence between left
$\mathcal D_\kappa$-modules and left $\mathcal D_{\kappa+\eta}$-modules.

manifest_record.title: The spin factor and the plus-quadratic Clifford convention

references.title: John C. Baez, The Octonions, arXiv:math/0105155v4 (2002)
N. Jacobson, Lectures on Quadratic Jordan Algebras, Tata Institute of Fundamental Research, 1969

manifest_record.statement: Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, let $Q(v)=\langle v,v\rangle$, and use the plus-$Q$ Clifford algebra $\mathrm{Cl}^{+}(V,Q)$ of [[def-clifford-algebra-of-a-quadratic-space]]. The map $\Phi:S(V)\to \mathrm{Cl}^{+}(V,Q)^+$, $\Phi(v,\alpha)=\bar v+\alpha 1$ is an injective unital Jordan homomorphism onto the Jordan subalgebra $\mathbb R1+\bar V$. In particular, $\bar v\bar w+\bar w\bar v=2\langle v,w\rangle1$. The spin-factor square cone is exactly $\{(v,\alpha):\alpha\geq\|v\|\}$, whose boundary is the future null cone $\{(v,\alpha):\alpha\geq0,\ \alpha^2-\|v\|^2=0\}$ of $q(v,\alpha)=\alpha^2-\|v\|^2$.

manifest_record.title: The formal Bernstein presentation for a reduced based root datum
manifest_record.statement:
Let $R=(X,\Phi,Y,\Phi^\vee,\Delta)$ be as in [[def-abstract-root-datum-and-its-weyl-group]], with finite Weyl group $W_0$. Use the finite simple-reflection set $S_0=\{s_\alpha:\alpha\in\Delta\}$ specified in [[def-hh-affine-hecke-algebra-from-root-datum]], where $S_0$ generates $W_0$ and is contained in $S_{\mathrm{aff}}$. For $s,t\in S_0$, let $m(s,t)$ be the order of $st$ in $W_0$, which is finite because $W_0$ is finite. The group algebra $\mathbb C[Y]$ is the complex vector space with basis $\{\theta_y:y\in Y\}$ and multiplication $\theta_y\theta_z=\theta_{y+z}$; its identity is $\theta_0$. The simple reflection corresponding to $\alpha\in\Delta$ acts on $Y$ by $s_\alpha(y)=y-\langle\alpha,y\rangle\alpha^\vee$.

Write $2X=\{2x:x\in X\}$. For each simple root $\alpha\in\Delta\cap2X$, also supply a positive scalar $v'_\alpha$; it is the second parameter in the doubled-root rank-one Bernstein relation. This additional scalar is formal input to the presentation. To compare this presentation with a specified $\mathcal H_{\mathrm{IM}}(R,q)$, its parameters must be **attached**: require $v'_\alpha=v(H_{\alpha,1})$, where $v(H)$ is the positive square root of the parameter of its wall reflection, well defined by [[lem-hh-root-datum-affine-geometry-and-wall-parameters]]. The finite parameter is already $v_\alpha=v(H_{\alpha,0})$. Without this tie one is defining a formal Bernstein algebra, not asserting comparison with the fixed $q$. When $\alpha\notin2X$, no second parameter is used; the wall-parameter lemma proves the two wall classes have equal parameters.

Define the **formal Bernstein algebra** $\mathcal B(R,v,v')$ as the quotient of the free associative $\mathbb C$-algebra on $\{\theta_y:y\in Y\}$ and $\{N_s:s\in S_0\}$ by $\theta_0=1$, $\theta_y\theta_z=\theta_{y+z}$ for $y,z\in Y$, the finite Hecke relations, and the following cross-relation for each $\alpha\in\Delta$ and $y\in Y$. Here $v_\alpha:=v_{s_\alpha}=\sqrt{q_{s_\alpha}}>0$ from [[def-hh-affine-hecke-algebra-from-root-datum]], and the finite Hecke relations are $(N_s-v_s)(N_s+v_s^{-1})=0$ for $s\in S_0$ and equality of the alternating products of $N_s,N_t$ of length $m(s,t)$ for distinct $s,t\in S_0$ ([[def-hh-universal-coxeter-hecke-parameters-and-presentation]]):

$$
\theta_yN_{s_\alpha}-N_{s_\alpha}\theta_{s_\alpha(y)}=\begin{cases}(v_\alpha-v_\alpha^{-1})\dfrac{\theta_y-\theta_{s_\alpha(y)}}{1-\theta_{-\alpha^\vee}},&\alpha\notin2X,\\[1ex]\bigl((v_\alpha-v_\alpha^{-1})+\theta_{-\alpha^\vee}(v'_\alpha-(v'_\alpha)^{-1})\bigr)\dfrac{\theta_y-\theta_{s_\alpha(y)}}{1-\theta_{-2\alpha^\vee}},&\alpha\in2X.\end{cases}
$$

The quotients are interpreted in $\mathbb C[Y]$; their well-definedness is proved in [[lem-hh-affine-hecke-bernstein-quotients-are-well-defined]]. The quotient construction defines an associative algebra. It does **not** assert that $\mathcal B(R,v,v')$ is nonzero, has a PBW basis, or is isomorphic to the Iwahori–Matsumoto algebra of [[def-hh-affine-hecke-algebra-from-root-datum]].
manifest_record.strategy: State the root-datum conventions, parameter normalization, two Bernstein cross-relations, and quotient presentation; claim no PBW basis or equivalence to the Iwahori–Matsumoto algebra in the definition.
manifest_record.axiom_use: None; a quotient of a free associative algebra is defined without a choice principle.

manifest_record.statement:

$$
\frac{\theta_y-\theta_{s_\alpha(y)}}{1-\theta_{-\alpha^\vee}}\in\mathbb C[Y]\quad\text{if }\alpha\notin2X,

\frac{\theta_y-\theta_{s_\alpha(y)}}{1-\theta_{-2\alpha^\vee}}\in\mathbb C[Y]\quad\text{if }\alpha\in2X.
$$

manifest_record.title: The Green Hall completion and coproduct

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, Hall algebras and quantum groups, Inventiones Mathematicae 101 (1990), 583–591
references.locator: §1, printed pp. 585–586: composition-algebra flag counts (background only). The Green coproduct and tensor conventions are from Schiffmann §§1.4–1.5, cited above.

manifest_record.statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite-field hereditary Hall category and use
$H_{\mathcal A,\nu}$ and the object-level integer $\chi_0(M,N)$ from
[[def-euler-twisted-hall-algebra]]. For a basis object $R$, let
$P^R_{M,N}$ count endpoint-labelled exact sequences
$0\to N\to R\to M\to0$, and put $a_R=|\operatorname{Aut}(R)|$. Define the
**coefficientwise completed tensor space**
$$ H_{\mathcal A,\nu}\widehat\otimes H_{\mathcal A,\nu} =\prod_{([M],[N])}\mathbb Q(\nu)\,([M]\otimes[N]), $$
the space of all coefficient functions on ordered pairs of isomorphism
classes. Define the Green coproduct and counit by
$$ \Delta'([R])=\sum_{[M],[N]} \nu^{\chi_0(M,N)}\frac{P^R_{M,N}}{a_R}[M]\otimes[N], \qquad \epsilon([R])=\begin{cases}1,&R\cong0,\\0,&R\not\cong0.\end{cases} $$
Each coefficient is finite; the sum need not have finite support. On finite
pure tensors define the **Euler-twisted tensor multiplication** by
$$ ([X]\otimes[Y])\cdot([Z]\otimes[W]) =\nu^{\chi_0(Y,Z)+\chi_0(Z,Y)}([X]\star[Z])\otimes([Y]\star[W]). $$
It is extended to completed tensors only when every output coefficient is a
finite sum. No algebra structure on the whole completion is asserted; this
finite-convergence condition is proved for products of Green images below.

subject: cor-extended-green-hall-bialgebra

manifest_record.title: The extended Green coproduct is an algebra map

references.title: Olivier Schiffmann, Lectures on Hall Algebras, arXiv:math/0611617v2
Claus Michael Ringel, Hall algebras and quantum groups, Inventiones Mathematicae 101 (1990), 583–591
references.locator: §3, printed pp. 588–589: adjunction of Cartan derivations (background only). The extended Green coproduct is from Schiffmann §1.5, Corollary 1.10, cited above.

manifest_record.statement:
For the extended Hall algebra of
[[def-extended-hall-algebra-and-composition-subalgebra]], define
$\Delta_-(k_\alpha)=k_\alpha\otimes k_\alpha$ and, for homogeneous $[R]$,
$$ \Delta_-([R]) =\sum_{[M],[N]}\nu^{\langle M,N\rangle} \frac{P^R_{M,N}}{a_R}\,[M]\otimes k_{-[M]}[N]. $$
Then $\Delta_-$ is an algebra map into the coefficientwise completed tensor
space of the extended Hall algebra, with ordinary (untwisted) tensor
multiplication on the coproduct images, whose coefficient sums converge.
The counit is an algebra map to the coefficient field. If every basis
coproduct has finite support, these maps define an ordinary tensor-product
bialgebra; otherwise their target is the stated completion. This is the **DJ-compatible extended Green convention** used on this
page. The alternative formula
$\Delta_+([R])=\sum c^R_{M,N}[M]k_{[N]}\otimes[N]$ has
$\Delta_+([S_i])=[S_i]\otimes1+k_i\otimes[S_i]$ and is kept separate.
manifest_record.strategy: Check the group-like and Hall generators and use the torus action to convert the twisted tensor factor into the extended tensor product.
